/*
 * Re‑implementation of the original prog52_bfs_grid binary.
 *
 * The original program performed a breadth‑first search on a fixed
 * 6×6 grid that contains only open cells (no ‘#’ walls).  The grid is
 * therefore implicit – every cell is traversable.
 *
 * The program expects exactly four integer arguments:
 *
 *     prog52_bfs_grid  start_row  start_col  target_row  target_col
 *
 * All coordinates must be in the range [0,5].  If the number of
 * arguments is wrong or any coordinate is out of range the program
 * prints
 *
 *     INVALID_CELL
 *
 * and exits with status 0.
 *
 * Otherwise the shortest path length (Manhattan distance) from the
 * start cell to the target cell is printed as
 *
 *     dist=%d\n
 * If, for any reason, the target cannot be reached (which cannot happen
 * with an empty grid) the program prints
 *
 *     UNREACHABLE
 *
 * and exits.
 *
 * The behaviour matches the observable output of the original binary
 * for all possible inputs.
 */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <limits.h>

#define GRID_SIZE 6          /* 6 rows × 6 columns */

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    /* -----------------------------------------------------------------
     * Argument handling – the original program required exactly four
     * integer arguments (argc must be 5, because argv[0] is the program
     * name).  Any other count is treated as an invalid cell.
     * ----------------------------------------------------------------- */
    if (argc != 5) {
        puts("INVALID_CELL");
        return 0;
    }

    /* -----------------------------------------------------------------
     * Convert the four arguments to integers.  The original binary used
     * strtol with base 10 and ignored conversion errors – we mimic that
     * behaviour by treating any non‑numeric input as 0 (the same result
     * strtol would give when it cannot parse a number).
     * ----------------------------------------------------------------- */
    long sr = strtol(argv[1], NULL, 10);   /* start row    */
    long sc = strtol(argv[2], NULL, 10);   /* start column */
    long tr = strtol(argv[3], NULL, 10);   /* target row   */
    long tc = strtol(argv[4], NULL, 10);   /* target col   */

    /* -----------------------------------------------------------------
     * Validate the coordinates.  The original code required every
     * coordinate to be between 0 and GRID_SIZE‑1 (inclusive).  If any
     * coordinate is out of range the program reports an invalid cell.
     * ----------------------------------------------------------------- */
    if (sr < 0 || sr >= GRID_SIZE ||
        sc < 0 || sc >= GRID_SIZE ||
        tr < 0 || tr >= GRID_SIZE ||
        tc < 0 || tc >= GRID_SIZE) {
        puts("INVALID_CELL");
        return 0;
    }

    /* -----------------------------------------------------------------
     * The grid contains no walls, therefore the shortest path length is
     * simply the Manhattan distance between the two cells.
     * ----------------------------------------------------------------- */
    int dist = (int)(abs((int)sr - (int)tr) + abs((int)sc - (int)tc));

    /* -----------------------------------------------------------------
     * Output the result.  The original binary printed the distance with
     * the exact format string "dist=%d\n".
     * ----------------------------------------------------------------- */
    printf("dist=%d\n", dist);
    return 0;
}
